the design and implementation of 28GHz phased arrays in CMOS for 4G/5G mobile user equipment and basestation applications.
the design of phased array transceivers in CMOS for 28GHz 5G applications.
the development of a 28GHz phased-array transceiver in bulk CMOS for 802.11ay and 5G applications.

this paper demonstrates the feasibility of a 28GHz phased-array transceiver in 28 nm CMOS for 4G/5G mobile user equipment and basestation applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a 28nm CMOS 28GHz phased-array transceiver with RF-IF conversion, that is capable of supporting a 12 element array with 2 MIMO streams.

we have designed a 28GHz phased-array transceiver with RF-to-IF conversion in 0.28μm bulk CMOS that can support 12 antennas per MIMO layer and can be tiled to support larger antenna arrays for base-stations.

we have designed and demonstrated a complete transceiver for 5G millimeter wave applications, including RF, IF, and baseband, and have demonstrated the transceiver in a small form factor, which is suitable for a 5G user terminal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 5G prototype user equipment with a 12-element phased array can be implemented in bulk CMOS.

a 28GHz phasedarray transceiver with 12 antennas in 28nm CMOS can be designed with reasonable complexity, and that the transceiver can be used to support both UE and basestations in a 5G phased array system.
28nm CMOS is a viable technology choice for phased array transceivers in 28GHz 5G systems.
